extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the ideal courtier on speaking, writing, deportment, and learning — covering rhetorical style, voice and gesture, moral character, language usage, and literary education. Advice is aimed at comporting oneself gracefully and effectively at court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge as foundation for speech and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Courtier must have knowledge; he who is ignorant and has nothing in his mind that merits being heard can neither say it nor write it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thought must precede words — 'to divide thought from words is to divide soul from body.' Substantive, beautiful, ingenious, acute, elegant and grave thoughts are necessary for praise and effective speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly arrangement of material
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange in good order what one has to say or write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before expression, the courtier should organize ideas clearly so that speech or writing presents thought coherently and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise, choice, rich, rightly formed words
rubrics_metrics.description: Words ought to be precise, choice, rich and rightly formed, but above all in use even among the masses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose words most expressive of meaning, 'exalt them, to mould them like wax to his will,' and arrange them so their dignity and splendour show at a glance — like pictures placed in proper light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use language accessible to listeners
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer words that are in use among the masses so the speaker will be understood by everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facility is not an impediment to elegance; a courtier's elegance should coexist with general understandability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocal qualities for speaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice should be sonorous, clear, sweet and well sounding; not too thin and soft nor too stern and rough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produced voice must be pleasant and fitting to public address; avoid extremes that betray weakness or rusticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct enunciation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity of articulation is required so each word and nuance of meaning is conveyed to listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper bearing and natural gestures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper bearing and gestures consist in certain movements of the whole body, not affected or violent, but tempered by a calm face and a play of the eyes giving an effect of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gestures should accord with the words and, so far as possible, express the speaker's intent and feeling; avoid affected or violent motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance over ornament — beautiful thoughts necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: All manner of verbal excellence is vain if the thoughts expressed are not beautiful, ingenious, acute, elegant and grave according to the need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style must reflect substantive thought; rhetorical flourish cannot compensate for poor ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of subject and tonal flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Speak and write of amusing things, games, jests and waggery when occasion, but sensibly of everything, with readiness and lucid fullness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A courtier should be adaptable: know when to be light or grave; avoid vanity and childish folly; be quick and full in expression appropriate to subject and occasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on obscure or difficult subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: When speaking on an obscure or difficult subject, carefully explain meaning with precision of both word and thought, and make every ambiguity clear and plain with a certain touch of unpedantic care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain rather than obscure: remove ambiguity gently and without pedantry so listeners understand complex points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to move and modulate emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Know how to speak with dignity and force to arouse emotions, and also how to soften them with simple candour to intoxicate them with sweetness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhetorical force to kindle or move emotions as needed, but also temper with sweetness so listeners feel both power and ease; make excellence seem attainable to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employing regional and foreign terms when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Not only choose rich and elegant words from every part of Italy, but sometimes use French and Spanish terms already accepted by custom, provided he might hope to be understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of dialectal or foreign words can enrich speech/style if they are understood; examples given (e.g., 'pritnor', 'aventurare') illustrate tasteful borrowing when intelligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative yet tasteful word usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes use words in a sense other than proper to them, transpose them aptly, graft them like branches, and form new words and figures of speech tastefully from the Latins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metaphorical transposition and neologism are allowed if they make expression more attractive and bring things into vivid view; draw tastefully from Latin tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for living usage and good custom
rubrics_metrics.description: Good custom in speech springs from men with talent and good judgment who accept words that seem good — recognized by innate judgment and usage rather than by artificial rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid needlessly imposing artificial laws or excessive antiquarianism; usage evolves and 'figures of speech' that infringe grammar can be accepted by custom because they give pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek ease, good order, richness, beautiful sentences and harmonious periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain things are always good in every language: ease, good order, richness, beautiful sentences, harmonious periods; affectation is bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for naturalness and harmony in phrasing; avoid affectation and artificiality which destroy grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and nonchalance as sources of grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Affectation imparts ungracefulness while simplicity and nonchalance produce the height of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonchalant simplicity—appearing natural rather than forced—creates charm (illustrated by minimal cosmetics, natural gestures, modest display).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid showing off or excessive display
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not show vanity or childish folly; many graceful things are most pleasing when hidden or displayed sparingly (e.g., modest makeup, rarely-seen elegant shoes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtlety and restraint increase perceived naturalness and elegance; ostentation betrays artifice and loses grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral character as essential qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: The Courtier should be an honest and upright man; in this are included prudence, goodness, strength and temperance of mind, and all other appropriate qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goodness is primary; moral desire to be good is the core of true moral philosophy and underpins outward accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters and humanities as principal ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters are the true and principal ornament of the mind; the Courtier should be more than passably accomplished in letters, especially in the humanities and conversant with Latin and Greek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be well versed in poets, orators, historians, and proficient in writing verse and prose (especially the vernacular). If unable to reach high perfection, suppress inferior writings and share only with trusted friends; practice writing to better judge others' work.
